cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: 5 years of cash flows, 10% finance rate, 12% reinvestment rate
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 12.61% (the live page displays it rounded to 13%). Independently derived from the documented formula MIRR = (-NPV(reinvest, positives)*(1+reinvest)^n / (NPV(finance, negatives)*(1+finance)))^(1/(n-1)) - 1 with n = 6 values: the reinvested inflows are carried forward at 12% and the single -120000 outflow discounted at 10%; the 5th root of the ratio gives 0.12609413 -> 0.1261 at 4 dp

cases.description: Same doc example truncated to the first three years of inflows, which is still a net loss
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes this example's result as -4.80% (displayed rounded to -5%). Same formula with n = 4 values (-120000, 39000, 30000, 21000): the reinvested inflows do not recover the outflow, so the cube root of the ratio is below 1 -> -0.04804466 -> -0.048 at 4 dp

cases.description: Same cash flows with the reinvestment rate raised from 12% to 14%
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes this example's result as 13.48% (displayed rounded to 13%). Raising only the reinvestment rate raises the future value of the positive flows; recomputing the documented formula gives 0.13475911 -> 0.1348 at 4 dp

cases.description: A zero cash flow is neither an inflow nor an outflow, so it only contributes to the period count
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that MIRR ignores text, logical values and empty cells in a reference but INCLUDES cells with the value zero. Zero belongs to neither the positive nor the negative NPV; with finance = reinvest = 0.1, the future value of the inflows is 600*1.1 + 700 = 1360 and the compounded present value of the outflow is -1000, with n = 4 values, so (1360/1000)^(1/3) - 1 = 0.10793165 -> 0.1079

cases.description: Excel documents #DIV/0! when values contains no negative (or no positive) number
cases.expected_note: With no negative cash flow the denominator NPV of the outflows is zero, and Excel documents that MIRR requires at least one positive and one negative value or it returns #DIV/0!
